vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-4176
vulnerability.description: Perl heap overflow; fixed upstream in 5.43.9 / 5.42.2-rc1 / 5.40.4-rc1

statements.impact_statement: nixpkgs applies the upstream fix as a source patch without a version bump: pkgs/development/interpreters/perl/interpreter.nix references CVE-2026-4176 on nixos-26.05 and nixos-unstable (backported via NixOS/nixpkgs PR #528021). The perl 5.42.0 shipped in these images is built from that patched expression, so the version-only match is a false positive. NOT valid for images built from nixos-25.05/25.11, which never received the backport — this statement was added together with the base ref bump to nixos-26.05.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-13221
vulnerability.description: Perl through 5.43.9 produces silently INCORRECT regex matches when an alternation of >65535 fixed-string branches compiles into a trie (Perl_study_chunk 16-bit field overflow). False positives AND false negatives; no debugging pragma required.

statements.action_statement: RETRACTION. A previous revision of this document (v3) asserted not_affected with justification vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path. THAT WAS WRONG and the suppression has been removed. The error: the not_affected claim rested on the defect requiring the `use re "Debug"` pragma to trigger. It does not. The authoritative CVE record states Perl "produce[s] silently incorrect regular expression matches" — false positive AND false negative matches — and that "when such a pattern gates an access or filtering decision, the result is wrong". The pragma only converts the silent miscompilation into a visible "regexp memory corruption" abort, which is why the upstream GitHub report describes a crash. Local experiments that found "no crash without the pragma" were testing for the crash symptom, not for incorrect matching, and therefore never tested the actual vulnerability. The 73-script `perl -c -Mre=Debug` audit recorded in security/evidence/ has the same defect of premise: it detects the abort, so it cannot establish absence of silent miscompilation. CURRENT STATE OF THIS IMAGE. Two perl 5.42.0 interpreters ship: yp5hpzyy1b73b134jhm20avjhgmyj3py-perl-5.42.0 carries the upstream fix (Perl/perl5 03f74bbb) and is what exiftool's shebang resolves to — that consumer is FIXED, verified in the pulled image. haxjvirj4hk92rpjhx0qygqsf3a5iimz-perl-5.42.0 is UNPATCHED, executable, and on PATH for the ~70 other perl scripts in the image (libwww-perl, File-MimeInfo, XML-Twig, IO-Compress, perl core tools). A third, k7kxg101ikkm0cyf8jcqhg948vy542af-perl-5.42.0, is in the `services` closure. REQUIRED ACTION: patch or remove the unpatched interpreters, OR obtain explicit documented risk acceptance. Risk context for that decision, NOT offered as a suppression: this is a Kasm workspace in which the tenant already has terminal access and arbitrary same-uid code execution, so no privilege boundary is crossed by a tenant miscompiling their own regex; the realistic harm is a wrong answer from an OSINT tool the tenant is themselves operating. That is a materially different argument from "not affected" and must be recorded as acceptance, not suppression.
statements.impact_statement: Affected. Retains the evidence that exiftool's interpreter specifically is remediated (overlay build m4wc48yxm0cxiip44pyplspwgpxf6l2q-perl5.42.0-Image-ExifTool-13.59, shebang -> yp5hpzyy..., upstream reproducer rc=0 inside the shipped image where the unpatched interpreter exits rc=255). That does not clear the image, because the unpatched interpreters remain executable.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-8376
vulnerability.description: Perl through 5.43.10 heap buffer overflow compiling a repeated fixed string — 32-BIT BUILDS ONLY (Perl_study_chunk sized a buffer in characters not bytes)

statements.impact_statement: TWO independent grounds, either sufficient. (1) ARCHITECTURE. The authoritative CVE record scopes this to 32-bit builds: the overflow requires `mincount * l` to overflow SSize_t, which cannot occur on a 64-bit SSize_t. Every image in this catalog is built for x86_64 (bin/nix-profiles.toml declares platforms amd64; no i686/armv7 target exists in the pipeline). The vulnerable code path is unreachable on a 64-bit build regardless of input. (2) PATCHED ANYWAY. nixpkgs applies CVE-2026-8376.patch to perl 5.42.0. Verified at the exact revision this catalog builds from: `nix eval` of perl.patches at 531670d871c0e29724a02f3cbcac170adc65b58c returns ["no-sys-dirs.patch","CVE-2026-8376.patch"]. The scanner reports it unfixed only because the version string does not move for a distro backport. Catalog-wide rather than profile-scoped because both grounds are properties of the build (architecture, and the nixpkgs revision) rather than of any one profile's consumers. Re-verify ground (2) if the catalog ever pins a nixpkgs revision that drops the patch; ground (1) fails only if a 32-bit target is ever added.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-7598
vulnerability.description: libssh2 <= 1.11.1 integer overflow in userauth_password / userauth_list (src/userauth.c) via username_len/password_len

statements.impact_statement: nixpkgs backports the upstream fix without moving the version string, so a version-matching scanner cannot see it. The CVE lists NO fixed release — 1.11.1 is the latest and is itself listed as affected — which is why the scanner reports 'no fix available' rather than a version to move to. Upstream fix: libssh2/libssh2 commit 256d04b60d80bf1190e96b0ad1e91b2174d744b1 (PR #1858), adding UINT32_MAX bounds checks before the username_len + 27 and username_len + 40 allocations and correcting the existing username_len + password_len + 44 check to avoid the overflow it was meant to prevent. nixpkgs applies it as pkgs/by-name/li/libssh2/CVE-2026-7598.patch — verified by `nix eval` of libssh2.patches at revision 531670d871c0e29724a02f3cbcac170adc65b58c, which returns CVE-2026-7598.patch alongside CVE-2025-15661, CVE-2026-55199 and CVE-2026-55200. CONFIRMED IN THE SHIPPED BINARIES, not just in the expression. The patch introduces the literal error string "username_len out of bounds", which exists in NO unpatched build. All three libssh2 1.11.1 store paths present in the tracelabs image contain it: d9c9w2y52gffj7zz1b76j0f8fbp5ww4d (services closure), xhmdqv811ljip7ci70cv78r1iaflp5iy and zzq7pa15jb9bip5yhl7cdjr3wx5xhra2 (tracelabs closure). That includes the copy in the services closure, which is built from the overlay's older committed lock — so this holds even where the stale-pin defect applies. NOTE for reviewers: the presence of libssh2_userauth_password symbols in libcurl, and SFTP/SCP being compiled in, show only that the code path EXISTS. They are not evidence of exposure and were briefly misread as such during this triage; the applied-patch check is what settles it.
